cards.title: Telephone & Enquiry Handling
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- answer the phone warmly and promptly
- take accurate details and confirm them
- log and follow up every enquiry

cards.title: The first impression
cards.body: The phone is very often a guest's first contact with Black Horse Beamish. It might be a wedding enquiry, a table booking or a question about a stay. A first impression forms in seconds, and a warm, professional call can be the difference between winning a booking and losing it to somewhere that answered better.

cards.title: Quickly, warmly, by name
cards.body: Answer promptly, within a few rings, with a clear, friendly greeting and the venue name, so the caller knows they have reached the right place. Smile while you speak. It sounds odd, but a smile carries down the line and makes you sound warm rather than flat.

items.title: Venue name
items.text: So they know they have the right place.

cards.title: Take accurate notes
cards.body: Listen properly and take accurate notes. Get the key details and repeat them back to confirm you have got them right.

cards.title: Answer it or hand it on
cards.body: Never leave an enquiry hanging. Either answer it fully or tell the caller exactly who will get back to them and when.

left.title: Do
items: Say who will get back to them
Say when they will hear back

right.title: Do not
items: Leave it because you are busy

cards.title: Do not let it slip
cards.body: Follow up when you say you will. Make sure enquiries, especially for weddings and events, are logged properly so they do not slip through the cracks. A missed or forgotten enquiry is a lost booking and a poor impression.

items.title: Start well
items.text: A good call starts the guest's whole experience on a high.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Answer within a few rings with a friendly greeting and the venue name
- Smile while you speak
- Take notes, repeat key details back, always take a name and number
- Never leave an enquiry hanging: say who will call back and when
- Log enquiries and follow up when you say you will

cards.q: You should answer the phone within…
options: A minute or so
Ten rings
Once the other call finishes
A few rings
cards.why: Answer promptly, within a few rings.

cards.q: Smiling while you speak makes you sound warmer on the phone.
cards.why: A smile really does carry down the line and makes you sound warm and welcoming rather than flat.

cards.q: Why should you repeat key details back to the caller?
options: It gives you time to think
To confirm you have got them right
It makes the call longer
So the caller can change their mind
cards.why: Repeating key details back confirms you have got them right.

cards.q: The phone is often a guest's very first contact with the venue.
cards.why: A wedding enquiry, table booking or stay question often starts with a call, and the first impression is formed in seconds.

cards.q: You should always take the caller's…
options: Star sign and birthday
Home address and employer
Name and contact number
Bank details and PIN
cards.why: Always take the caller's name and a contact number so nothing is lost.

cards.q: It is fine to leave an enquiry hanging if you are busy.
cards.why: Never leave an enquiry hanging. Answer fully or say who will get back to them and when.

cards.q: Why is it important to log wedding and event enquiries properly?
options: It looks tidy in the diary
So no enquiry is lost or forgotten
So the phone bill is accurate
So guests can be charged for calling
cards.why: Enquiries that are not logged can slip through the cracks, and a forgotten enquiry is a lost booking.

options: Just "hello" and the question
Your full name and job title
Nothing, to save time on the call
A friendly greeting and the venue name
cards.why: A clear, friendly greeting and the venue name tell the caller they have reached the right place.

cards.q: A forgotten enquiry can mean a lost booking.
cards.why: A missed or forgotten enquiry is a lost booking and a poor impression.

cards.q: If you cannot answer the enquiry yourself, what should you tell the caller?
options: That they should try again later on
That the venue is too busy right now
Who will get back to them and when
That someone will be in touch soon
cards.why: Tell them exactly who will get back to them and when, so the enquiry is never left hanging.
